conventions: Versification split between 1TH.1.2 and 1TH.1.3 under rule 37: the projection carries ἀδιαλείπτως at the end of 1:2 (s015) and the ASV translates it at the head of 1:3 as *without ceasing*. 1:2 leaves the adverb `unrepresented`, 1:3 marks the two English words `added`, and neither verse reaches across. Do not fold *without ceasing* onto μνημονεύοντες, and do not stretch ἀδιαλείπτως onto ποιούμενοι. A reference comparison reports the adverb as a disagreement, and that report is not a correction.

1TH.1.5 carries two adjacent ἐν tokens (s014, s015) against a single English *in* before *power*, because two textual units overlap there: SBLGNT.1TH.1.5.v004 selected r01, which supplies καὶ ἐν, and SBLGNT.1TH.1.5.v005 selected r00-base, which supplies ἐν δυνάμει. The one *in* is given to s014, the token r01 introduced along with the καί the ASV renders *but also*, and s015 stands as its own `unrepresented` unit under rule 97's mirror case, the projection carrying more source material than the ASV rendered. Reversing the two would be equally defensible. This is an artifact of overlapping variant units rather than a contract question, and the BSB comparison's report of the empty ἐν is not a correction.

promotions.summary: Settles the target head for an intensive αὐτός that the ASV renders by a two-word English emphatic — *he himself*, *they themselves*, *I myself*, *his own self* — on the *-self* word rather than on the plain pronoun in front of it, and denies that the choice is the genuine tie rule 17 lets English syntax break. 1TH.1.9's αὐτοὶ → *they themselves* is this chapter's instance and the corpus's first plural one.
promotions.basis: Corpus query LEMMA=αὐτός TARGET='self', this chapter excluded: thirteen units head the *-self* word — ten of *he himself* → *himself*, PHP.2.24 *I myself* → *myself*, 1PE.2.24 *his own self* → *self*, ROM.16.2 *own self* → *self* — against four heading the plain pronoun. Of those four, JHN.6.6 is `medium` and concedes *himself* in its own note, MRK.10.12 concedes *herself*, ROM.16.2 heads its own second αὐτός on *self* in the same verse, and only REV.19.12 argues the point, resting it on a tie between the two words. That is rule 71's shape — one contested reading against an otherwise settled line — rather than rule 67's genuinely divided case, and the thirty-eight single-word *himself* units bear on nothing, the head being trivial there.
promotions.rule: An intensive `αὐτός` that the ASV renders by a **two-word English emphatic** is one `aligned` unit headed on the ***-self*** word, never on the plain pronoun standing in front of it. `αὐτοὶ` → *they themselves* heads on *themselves*, as `αὐτὸς` → *he himself* heads on *himself* in ten corpus units, `αὐτὸς` → *I myself* on *myself* at PHP.2.24, `αὐτὸς` → *his own self* on *self* at 1PE.2.24, and `αὐτοῦ` → *own self* on *self* at ROM.16.2; discontinuity changes nothing, HEB.2.14's *he … himself* being one unit under rule 15. Rule 17 is what decides it: the *-self* word is what realizes the intensive force the pronoun carries, while the *he*, *she*, *they* or *I* beside it is the subject word English syntax requires and rides inside the unit as a rule 7 or rule 9 helper. So this is not the genuine tie rule 17 lets English word order break, and a head on the plain pronoun is not a materially different analysis under rule 16. The corpus is thirteen units to four, and of the four JHN.6.6 and MRK.10.12 concede this reading in their own notes, ROM.16.2 heads its own second `αὐτός` on *self* in the same verse, and only REV.19.12 argues the point, on a tie this rule denies. Where the ASV writes a **single** English word the question does not arise and that word is the head, as the units of *himself*, *itself*, *myself*, *thyself* and *herself* are, and as `αὐτὸς` → *selfsame* is. An `αὐτός` carrying no intensive force is untouched by this rule: an oblique pronoun is aligned in the ordinary way, and a genitive one carries the English possessive and displaces its article under rule 20.

report: Checked all 16 candidate lemmas plus the two `added` units the candidate table is blind to. No cross-verse split found: every difference is licensed by the source or by the ASV's own phrasing, so patches is empty.

Articles. The ὁ groups differ only by what the ASV writes. τῇ → *unto the* (1:1), τοῦ → *of the* (1:6, 1:8) and τῶν/τῆς → *the* (1:10) each anchor a written determiner under rules 19 and 21; every `unrepresented` article is either rule 20 displacement, with ὑμῶν, ἡμῶν or αὐτοῦ present and unspent (1:2, 1:3 three times, 1:4, 1:5, 1:8, 1:10), or rule 23 with no determiner written (*to God*, *of faith*, *labor*, *of love*, *patience*, *of hope*, *unto God*, *from idols*, *heaven*, the names in 1:7–1:8, the second attributive τῆς in 1:10). The T→V bucket is not a split: τοῖς πιστεύουσιν (1:7) is substantival and takes the single relativizer under rule 90, while Ἰησοῦν τὸν ῥυόμενον (1:10) governs an expressed head noun and is emptied by rule 31. That is rule 31's own test, applied correctly both ways.

Anarthrous determiners are handled one way throughout, the supplied determiner going to the noun and discontinuously across an intervening adjective: πατρί → *the Father*, κυρίῳ → *the Lord*, Θεσσαλονικέων → *of the Thessalonians*, τύπον → *an ensample*, πνεύματι ἁγίῳ → *the … Spirit*, πνεύματος ἁγίου → *of the … Spirit*, θεῷ ζῶντι καὶ ἀληθινῷ → *a … God*. That is rules 51 and 58 with nothing added, so it needs no convention.

Other pairs checked and found licensed: ὥστε → *so that* headed on *so* at 1:7 and 1:8 against ὅτι → *how that* headed on *that* at 1:5, where *that* is the complementizer answering to the lexeme and *how* the archaic filler; πρὸς τὸν θεόν → *to God-ward* (1:8) against *unto God* (1:9), an ASV phrasing difference with both articles empty under rule 23 either way; the three γίνομαι finites, where an expressed ὑμεῖς/ὑμᾶς takes the English subject (1:6, 1:7) and rule 9 supplies it inside the verb where none is expressed (1:5); the two *forth* particles of 1:8, both kept inside their compound verb under rule 106 with no expressed ἐκ in either clause to claim them; and οἷοι (1:5) with ὁποίαν (1:9), both headed on *what* under rule 99.

BSB: none of the six disagreements is an error. τῷ (1:2) and the three genitive-chain articles (1:3) are the documented rule 20/23 convention difference. ἀδιαλείπτως (1:2) is the rule 37 versification split, which rule 37 says a comparison will report and which the report is not a correction of. ἐν (1:5) is the duplicated preposition described in the second convention below, an artifact of two overlapping textual units rather than an alignment decision.

One gap I could not settle and did not paper over: 1TH.1.10's supplied appositional *even* before Ἰησοῦν falls in a carrier class rule 105 does not name — a bare accusative name, with neither an expressed preposition to fold onto nor a substantival article. The verse marks it `added` by analogy with rule 105's article arm and says so in its note. I asked for corpus evidence on αὐτός only, so this round cannot decide it, and I am not promoting a rule the corpus here does not speak to.
